title: Arm's AGI Data Center CPU at Hot Chips 2026
gist: Arm detailed AGI, its first complete commercial CPU sold directly to server vendors rather than as IP: two TSMC N3P chiplets with more than 50 billion transistors each, up to 136 Neoverse V3 cores at up to 3.7GHz in a 300W TDP, 12-channel DDR5-8800 for 845GB/s, 96 PCIe Gen6 lanes, and UCIe die-to-die at 1TB/s per direction. Arm chose N3P over N2 for proven performance, and frames AGI as the first step in a long-term chip roadmap.

themes.theme: Arm becomes a chip vendor, not just an IP licensor

insights.claim: Arm is breaking new ground by offering its own CPU directly to server vendors rather than just selling the IP, a significant change of pace that lets the company control its own destiny like never before.
insights.speaker: Ryan Smith
insights.so_what: Arm competing with its own licensees changes the risk calculus for every Neoverse customer and could accelerate RISC-V interest as a hedge.
insights.quote: Arm is breaking new ground by offering their own CPU directly to server vendors rather than just selling the IP. It is a significant change of pace for the company, and one that lets them control their own destiny like never before.
insights.locator: Continuing with our coverage of the second CPU session

insights.claim: AGI represents Arm's progression from designing IP, to designing entire compute subsystem blocks, to its first in-house commercial chip.
insights.speaker: Ryan Smith
insights.so_what: The IP-to-CSS-to-chip ladder is the path other IP vendors may follow, with each rung capturing more value per design win.
insights.quote: Over the years they have gone from designing IP, to designing entire compute subsystems (CSS) blocks, to now their first in-house commercial chip.
insights.locator: AGI has been a journey for Arm

insights.claim: AGI is the first part of a long-term hardware commitment, with Arm holding an extensive SoC roadmap for future generations of data center processors.
insights.speaker: Ryan Smith
insights.so_what: A sustained roadmap rather than a one-off means Arm's licensees face ongoing first-party competition, not a single experiment.
insights.quote: AGI is the first part of a long-term hardware commitment for Arm.

insights.claim: Arm will offer a reference server alongside multiple vendor designs spanning rack-scale systems down to traditional commercial servers.
insights.speaker: Ryan Smith
insights.so_what: A reference platform lowers the integration barrier for OEMs, accelerating time from silicon to shipping systems.
insights.locator: But there will be multiple vendor designs

insights.claim: Arm chose TSMC N3P for the AGI chiplets because it is a performance and proven process node, with the undertext being that Arm did not want to take a chance on, or did not have access to, an N2 node at this time.
insights.speaker: Ryan Smith
insights.so_what: Arm entering at N3P while Fujitsu and AMD use N2 means AGI concedes a node of efficiency, which matters in a 300W part.
insights.quote: The company picked N3P because it is a performance and proven process node, the undertext being that Arm didn’t want to take a chance on (or didn’t have access to) an N2 node at this time.
insights.locator: Arm opted for TSMC N3P for the AGI chiplets

insights.claim: Arm did not spend the gates or die area for higher frequencies because it wanted to maximize energy efficiency, capping cores at 3.7GHz.
insights.speaker: Ryan Smith
insights.so_what: Deliberately trading peak clock for efficiency positions AGI against throughput-per-watt buyers rather than single-thread-sensitive workloads.
insights.quote: Arm didn’t spend the gates or die area for higher frequencies as they wanted to maximize energy efficiency.
insights.locator: Each SoC can support up to 136 Neoverse V3 cores

insights.claim: There are more than 50 billion transistors per AGI chiplet.
insights.speaker: Ryan Smith
insights.so_what: Over 100 billion transistors across two chiplets puts AGI in the same silicon-content class as flagship x86 server parts.
insights.quote: There are more than 50 billion transistors per chiplet.
insights.locator: Arm opted for TSMC N3P for the AGI chiplets

insights.claim: The AGI SoC supports up to 136 Neoverse V3 cores while carrying 144 cores in hardware, with the remainder reserved for die harvesting.
insights.speaker: Ryan Smith
insights.so_what: Eight spare cores of harvesting headroom is a yield strategy that keeps a large chiplet economically viable at N3P.
insights.quote: There are 144 cores in hardware, but the remaining core are for die harvesting purposes.
insights.locator: Each SoC can support up to 136 Neoverse V3 cores

insights.claim: The 64 core AGI parts will be allowed to run at slightly higher frequencies, boosting as high as 3.7GHz with a 3.5GHz nominal, while higher core count chips run at a 3.2GHz nominal with a 3.5GHz max boost.
insights.speaker: Ryan Smith
insights.so_what: The frequency spread across SKUs is narrow, so per-core performance is nearly uniform regardless of core count purchased.
insights.locator: Looking a bit more at the specs

themes.theme: Chiplet interconnect designed to hide NUMA

insights.claim: AGI's dedicated die-to-die subsystem runs at 32Gbps per lane, designed to ensure the D2D connection is not a bottleneck and that the chip comes very close to functioning as a single monolithic chip.
insights.speaker: Ryan Smith
insights.so_what: Making two chiplets behave as one die removes the NUMA penalty that has plagued chiplet server CPUs, a real software-side advantage.
insights.quote: It runs at 32Gbps/lane, which is an incredibly high data rate, and is designed to ensure the D2D connection is not a bottleneck, and that the chip comes very close to functioning as a single monolithic chip.

insights.claim: Arm uses UCIe for the D2D subsystem with two x16 modules at 16 lanes of 32Gbps each, giving 1TB of bandwidth in each direction between dies, deliberately more D2D bandwidth than memory bandwidth in order to keep NUMA-1 mode performance high.
insights.speaker: Ryan Smith
insights.so_what: Provisioning D2D above memory bandwidth is a design rule worth applying when evaluating any multi-chiplet CPU's real-world scaling.
insights.quote: That allows for 1TB of bandwidth in each direction between the dies, and means there is more D2D bandwidth than memory bandwidth, in order to keep NUMA-1 mode performance high.
insights.locator: Arm is also using UCIe for their D2D subsystem

insights.claim: Each AGI chiplet holds 35 compute tiles of 2 CPU cores each in a mesh balancing CPU cores against memory, I/O, and die-to-die subsystems, built from Arm's Neoverse V3 CSS at 70 CPU cores per chiplet.
insights.speaker: Ryan Smith
insights.so_what: Two-core tiles on a mesh is the same structural pattern Arm licenses to hyperscalers, so AGI performance is a proxy for what Graviton-class designs achieve.

insights.claim: The Neoverse V3 core is designed for a balance between performance and power efficiency with a private 2MB L2 cache and a 128-bit SVE2 SIMD, hitting a minimum single-core performance target.
insights.speaker: Ryan Smith
insights.so_what: A 128-bit SVE2 width is modest for vector-heavy AI and HPC math, so AGI's case rests on core count and efficiency rather than per-core vector throughput.
insights.quote: The V3 core has a private 2MB L2 cache, and a 128-bit SVE2 SIMD.
insights.locator: The Neoverse V3 core is designed for a balance

insights.claim: A 12 channel DDR5 memory system allows for 845GB/second of bandwidth using DDR5-8800 at 1DPC, dropping to DDR5-6400 speeds at 2DPC.
insights.speaker: Ryan Smith
insights.so_what: The 1DPC-only path to peak bandwidth constrains memory capacity per socket, a real trade-off for memory-heavy tenants.
insights.quote: a 12 channel DDR5 memory system allows for 845GB/second of bandwidth using DDR5-8800. It can hit those speeds at 1DPC, while 2DPC drops to DDR5-6400 speeds.
insights.locator: Meanwhile, a 12 channel DDR5 memory system

insights.claim: Aggregate memory throughput is over 800GB/second, which works out to around 6GB/second per core.
insights.speaker: Ryan Smith
insights.so_what: Bandwidth per core is the comparison metric that exposes whether high-core-count CPUs are actually memory starved.
insights.quote: The aggregate memory throughput is over 800GB/second, which works out to around 6GB/second per core.
insights.locator: Each SoC can support up to 136 Neoverse V3 cores

insights.claim: Arm intends to match I/O bandwidth to memory bandwidth in its designs, providing six IO subsystems totaling 96 PCIe Gen6 lanes plus 6 Gen4 lanes for utility purposes, with bifurcation down to 4x4 and CXL 3.0 Type3 support.
insights.speaker: Ryan Smith
insights.so_what: Matching I/O to memory bandwidth is a stated design principle that predicts how Arm will scale future generations.
insights.quote: Arm intends to match I/O bandwidth to memory bandwidth in their designs.
insights.locator: Arm is also using UCIe for their D2D subsystem

insights.claim: AGI delivers up to 136 cores on a 300 Watt TDP with IPC and frequency at production goals and low memory latencies in a NUMA 2 configuration.
insights.speaker: Ryan Smith
insights.so_what: Roughly 2.2W per core at the top SKU is the efficiency figure Arm is asking server buyers to underwrite.
insights.quote: All of this is on a 300 Watt TDP. IPC and frequency is at their production goals.
insights.locator: All of this is on a 300 Watt TDP

insights.claim: Arm uses MPAM resource partitioning to ensure consistent chip performance and reduce starvation, and the hardware supports programmable page policies.
insights.speaker: Ryan Smith
insights.so_what: Consistent tenant performance under contention is what cloud providers require to sell guaranteed instance performance.
insights.locator: Diving a bit deeper, here is AGI’s memory subsystem

insights.claim: The CMN-S3 mesh must simultaneously scale across many CPU cores, carry a lot of memory bandwidth, and carry extensive I/O bandwidth for PCIe devices.
insights.speaker: Ryan Smith
insights.so_what: The mesh is the shared bottleneck across every Neoverse design, so its capabilities cap what all Arm server licensees can build.
insights.locator: The CMN-S3 mesh needs to meet multiple goals
